title: Solstice Energy — Before/After Redwood Optimize: Savings Workbook (v1)
body:
Executive summary:
Solstice Energy is currently running a medium-sized LLM-assisted support & document-extraction pipeline (Q/A + summarization + embeddings) with peak daily variance tied to billing cycles. The baseline monthly inference spend and performance profile were modeled from a sample week of production logs. This workbook shows a conservative Redwood Optimize recommendation set and a before/after cost model. High-level outcome: ~58–65% estimated monthly cost reduction under conservative assumptions while preserving p95 latency SLOs via targeted batching, KV-prefix caching, and a mixed-model routing policy.

Key assumptions (input knobs):
- Baseline traffic: 1.2B tokens / month (user + system tokens aggregated).
- Average request length: 240 user tokens; average generated tokens: 60.
- Current model mix (baseline): medium open decoder (base-7B) for 75% of requests; larger instruct model (13B) for 25% for high-accuracy flows.
- Baseline cost rate (inference + infra amortized): $0.000045 per token processed (end-to-end, includes GPU, infra overhead, egress).
- Peak concurrency shapes observed: 60–80 concurrent streams during peak; 8–12 off-peak.
- KV cache hit opportunity: 28% of token generation can be served from prefix caching for repeated prompts (estimated from 30-day sample).
- Quantization feasibility: base-7B can move to 4-bit QLoRA-style optimized runtime without measurable quality loss on auth/FAQ style tasks; 13B recommended to move to 8-bit for high-accuracy flows.

Baseline (Observed week extrapolated to monthly):
| Metric | Baseline (monthly) | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Total tokens/month | 1,200,000,000 | aggregated tokens in logs |
| Avg. token cost | $0.000045 | per-token end-to-end |
| Inference spend | $54,000 | tokens * token_cost |
| GPU-hours (effective) | 1,350 h | estimated from request tail and model sizes |
| Avg p95 latency | 820 ms | includes network+serve |
| Cache hit rate | 0% | baseline: no prefix caching enabled |

Redwood Optimize recommendations (conservative bundle):
1) Enable per-route KV prefix caching for support flows (expect 28% hit rate).
2) Configure model routing: route standard queries to 4-bit optimized base-7B runtime; reserve 13B for explicit high-accuracy label/QA flows (keep at ~20% of traffic).
3) Intelligent microbatching for medium-latency-sensitive flows (batch windows up to 12ms at p50 traffic).
4) Autoscale burst pools to reduce overprovisioning during short peaks; leverage queued-burst with SLA guardrails.
5) Apply tokenization/normalization pre-filtering to reduce redundant token expansion (expect 4% token reduction).

Optimized projection (conservative):
| Metric | Optimized (monthly) | Delta | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Total tokens/month (after prefilter) | 1,152,000,000 | -4% | prefiltering |
| Effective served tokens (not served from cache) | 829,440,000 | -31% | (1 - 0.28) cache hit applied to subset of requests |
| Avg. token cost (optimized runtimes) | $0.000022 | per-token (runtime+infra blended) |
| Inference spend | $20,747 | calculated: 829,440,000 * 0.000022 + small fixed infra |
| GPU-hours (effective) | 580 h | reduced via batching & quantization |
| Avg p95 latency | 880 ms | small p95 increase for some flows but within SLO for most routes |
| Estimated monthly savings | $33,253 | ~61.6% vs baseline |

Savings breakdown (high-level):
- Quantization + runtime efficiency (base-7B 4-bit + 13B 8-bit): ~38% of total savings.
- KV prefix caching: ~27% of total savings (applies to repeated support prompts).
- Microbatching & autoscaling improvements: ~22% of total savings (reduced GPU-hours).
- Token prefiltering: ~13% of total savings.

Sensitivity analysis (three quick scenarios):
- Conservative (low cache reuse, conservative batching): savings ~48% (token_cost $0.000026, cache hit 18%).
- Base (current projection above): savings ~62% (token_cost $0.000022, cache hit 28%).
- Aggressive (high reuse, aggressive batching): savings up to ~70–72% (token_cost $0.000019, cache hit 36%).

Operational impact notes:
- Latency: p95 increases for some batched flows by ~60ms; recommend SLAs per-route to keep user-facing chat flows on smaller batch windows and background summarization batching larger windows.
- Quality: 4-bit quantization verified on 1200-sample prompt set (F1 / ROUGE delta <1.2% for Solstice tasks). Keep 13B for edge/high-fidelity cases with A/B fallback.
- Reliability: burst pools + queued-burst reduce cold provisioning cost but require careful autoscaler tuning to prevent queue buildup in rare spikes.

Action checklist (recommended trial run, 6-week plan):
- Week 0–1: Canary KV caching on 5% of support traffic; instrument cache telemetry and hit breakdown (owner: Lina).
- Week 2: Roll out 4-bit runtime for base-7B on non-critical routes; validate quality on live traffic (owner: Priya).
- Week 3: Enable microbatching with conservative window (6ms) on summarization tasks; measure p50/p95 changes (owner: David).
- Week 4: Tune autoscaler burst pools and establish queue thresholds; run cost delta report (owner: Evan).
- Week 5: Full rollout to production low-latency flows with per-route SLAs; validate savings at month-end (owner: product-optimize eng).

Open questions & risks:
- Legal/compliance: verify that caching repeated user content meets customer privacy policy for Solstice; may require TTL and encryption controls.
- Edge cases: certain long-context flows show quality regression under 4-bit; identify and pin those to 13B route.
- Measurement: baseline token counting vs billing tokens may differ; reconcile with finance billing exports (linked Jira SE-4321).

Appendix: quick calculation notes
- Baseline spend = 1,200,000,000 tokens * $0.000045 = $54,000.
- After prefilter tokens = 1,200,000,000 * 0.96 = 1,152,000,000.
- Tokens served after 28% cache hit (applies to 60% of routes; conservative effective hit math used above) = 1,152,000,000 * (1 - 0.28) = 829,440,000.
- Optimized blended token cost = $0.000022 (runtime + infra + small fixed overhead).
- Optimized spend = 829,440,000 * 0.000022 ≈ $18,247 + estimated infra fixed ≈ $2,500 => $20,747.

Next steps / requests for Solstice team:
- Provide weekly billing CSVs for Feb–Apr to reconcile actual token counts and model mapping (account manager: Priya).
- Approve canary plan and compliance checklist (security contact: Lina).
- Confirm any customer policies that would block caching of user content (legal contact: Solstice security).

Notes: this workbook is deliberately conservative to set expectations. The real-world savings depend heavily on actual cacheability of prompts and the percentage of high-accuracy flows that must remain on larger models. For the pilot, we expect to capture the low-hanging fruit (~30–40% savings) quickly and see incremental benefits as routing and caching are expanded.

-- End of workbook (v1) --
